idiom_name: constructor function NewOrder(raw) (*Order, error) + functional options
implementation_notes: Go has no constructors, so the creation owner is the constructor function from Effective Go's constructors and composite literals section: func NewOrder(raw RawOrder) (*Order, error) validates, fills unexported fields and returns either a complete value or an error - never a half-built one, and callers cannot bypass it because the fields are unexported. That replaces the factory class entirely; when a creator must be selected or replaced (tests, tenant-specific builders), a function value or small interface does the job because functions are already first-class. When a creation path has many optional inputs, the community idiom is functional options (WithTimeout, WithMaxConns) applied inside the constructor, which keeps defaults in one place and the API extensible without breaking callers.
pitfalls: Exported structs with exported fields let callers build invalid values with a composite literal; keep invariant-bearing fields unexported or expose only an interface.
Mixing error contracts (nil value with nil error, or a value together with an error) breaks callers; pick one and document it.
Functional options that carry errors defer failures to the next method call; prefer error-returning options or validate after all options have been applied.
